text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your headache and vision changes, could you please describe the specific nature of the vision loss (e.g., blurred, double, or loss of peripheral vision) and whether the headache is constant or intermittent?

text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any jaw pain when chewing or scalp tenderness when brushing your hair? Additionally, have you noticed any redness or swelling in your temples?

text: Do you have any history of high blood pressure or diabetes, and have you noticed any sensitivity to light or nausea accompanying the headache?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any jaw pain when chewing or scalp tenderness, and has your vision loss affected one eye or both? REQUEST TEST: ESR

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ESR is normal, I need to rule out other causes like temporal arteritis or increased intracranial pressure. Have you noticed any jaw claudication or scalp tenderness, and is the vision loss affecting one eye or both? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: No acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass lesion identified. No evidence of increased intracranial pressure.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and ESR, I must investigate the optic nerve directly. Has your vision loss been in one eye or both, and have you experienced any pain when moving your eyes? REQUEST TEST: Optic Nerve Exam

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ophthalmologic Examination: Visual Acuity Right Eye 20/120, Left Eye 20/80. Fundoscopy: Findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopy findings suggest a vascular issue, so I need to assess your cardiovascular risk profile further. Do you have a history of atrial fibrillation or any known clotting disorders? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of atrial fibrillation or any known clotting disorders, and have you noticed any swelling or pain in your legs recently? REQUEST TEST: Carotid Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Carotid Ultrasound: No significant stenosis or plaque identified in the carotid arteries.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the retinal hemorrhages and your history of hypertension, I need to check your current blood pressure to rule out hypertensive retinopathy. REQUEST TEST: Blood Pressure Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
